'''Herman Louis Verlinde''' (born 21 January 1962) is a Dutch theoretical physicist and [[string theory|string theorist]]. He is the Class of 1909 Professor of Physics at [[Princeton University]], where he is also the chair of the Department of Physics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Herman L. Verlinde {{!}} Department of Physics |url=https://phy.princeton.edu/people/herman-l-verlinde |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=phy.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref> He is the [[identical twin]] brother of [[Erik Verlinde]].

== Life and work ==
Verlinde studied [[theoretical physics]] at [[Utrecht University]] and received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the same university, supervised by [[Gerard 't Hooft|Prof. Gerard 't Hooft]]. From 1995 to 1998, he was a full professor at the [[University of Amsterdam]], after which he was appointed full professor at [[Princeton University]].<ref name=":0" /> 

He specializes in [[string theory]] and [[quantum field theory]], and developed the [[Matrix string theory|Matrix String Theory]] together with his twin brother [[Erik Verlinde]] and [[Robbert Dijkgraaf]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dijkgraaf |first=R. |last2=Verlinde |first2=E. |last3=Verlinde |first3=H. |date= |year=1997 |title=Matrix String Theory |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9703030 |journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]] |volume=500 |issue=1-3 |pages=43–61 |doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(97)00326-X|arxiv=hep-th/9703030 }}</ref>
